text:
Happy Saturday! After that stretch of 60s and even 70s, today feels like November. We start cloudy and dry in the mid 40s, and the rain moves in around midday and gets steadier through the afternoon and evening. The high is 54. The European model is the wettest of the bunch, so I'd plan on the rain showing up. Keep the umbrella handy if you're out later.

Showers keep going overnight, tapering off around 5am Sunday, with a low near 39. All told, expect roughly a quarter to a half inch by the time it ends. The higher peaks could see a little slushy snow, but not Burlington.

Sunday starts damp, then dries out, and there's a decent shot at some sunshine late in the day. Highs land in the upper 40s to low 50s. The forecasters have it a bit warmer than the models, and I'd lean cooler. If you want a dry walk, wait for Sunday afternoon. Another lighter round of showers comes Monday.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: We await the arrival of showers this morning as a closed upper low slowly pivots eastward across the central/eastern Great Lakes. Scattered to numerous showers can already be seen out ahead of this feature. This area of showers will continue to slowly drift east-northeastward as its parent low crosses into southern NY, eventually pivoting into our southern sections along a weak inverted surface trough. This band of showers will rotate over NY through this afternoon before shifting east into VT late today and overnight as the upper low spins across southern New England and eventually offshore by Sunday morning. Hence expect fairly widespread showers through the day and into tonight, then becoming more focused in the northern mountains Sunday morning as west-northwest flow develops behind the departing low pressure. Snow levels drop to 2200-3200 ft as the cold pool moves overhead, and expect some slushy snow accumulation will be possible tonight into Sunday morning, generally above 2500 ft. Precipitation will wind down Sunday afternoon, with some sunshine possible by late in the day. Overall rainfall amounts will be a quarter to a half an inch, with locally higher amounts possible in the higher terrain. Temperatures will return to somewhat seasonal normals today and especially Sunday; highs in the 50s today will give way to mid 40s to mid 50s tomorrow. Winds may be a little on the breezy side in the Champlain Valley today as north winds get funneled down the valley. Strong winds then become more widespread on Sunday, though remaining AOB 25 mph or so, with little impact expected. KEY MESSAGE 2: Shortwave ridging briefly builds in behind the departing upper low, giving us a short respite from precipitation. However, another vigorous upper trough will swing along the international border Monday, with another following right in its footsteps on Tuesday. Showers will once again develop, though remaining more focused in the favored upslope areas of the northern Adirondacks/Greens as southwest winds shift to the west and eventually northwest. A reinforcing shot of cold air will see snow levels falling as low as 1500 ft early Tuesday morning, though the bulk of the precipitation will likely have ended by then, limiting potential snow accumulation. Total precipitation amounts will be a quarter of an inch or less through Monday night, with another tenth of two possible on Tuesday. Both days will see temperatures close to or just a bit above normal, generally in the mid 40s to low 50s. KEY MESSAGE 3: The large Hudson Bay low will continue to dominate the weather across our region, bringing multiple shortwaves into the weekend. A Shortwave pushes through on Tuesday bringing valley rain showers and some chances for snow to the upper terrain locations, mainly above 3000 feet AGL. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - The recent stretch of 60s and even 70s was very pleasant for being outdoors, and it felt like it was September again. However, it’s November, and it’s going to feel a lot more like it in the days to come. Today will start off early with mostly cloudy skies and a few showers, but rain will move in around mid-morning and continue through the day. It will be cooler with highs in the 50s. The rain will continue overnight, then move out from west to east Sunday morning. A half inch or more of rain is likely. However, a brief period of snow is possible in the Northeast Kingdom and Coos County, New Hampshire Sunday morning with 1 to 3 inches accumulation possible. The higher amounts will be at the summits of the White Mountains. The Northeast Kingdom could get an inch of snow, but it’s expected to melt pretty quickly once it hits the ground. Sunday afternoon will be partly sunny with highs in the 40s. Another system will bring additional rain on Monday, though it will be on the lighter side. Highs will be in the 40s and lows will be in the 30s. A few breaks of sun are possible on Tuesday, but scattered showers are likely, especially north. More widely scattered showers are expected on Veterans Day, though the mountains could get snow showers with colder highs in the upper 30s to low 40s. Dry weather is expected for Thursday and Friday, but temperatures will continue their downward trend. Thursday will be mostly cloudy, and Friday will be partly sunny. Highs will only be in the 30s to low 40s both days, so make sure to have a solid jacket if you head outdoors. Lows will be in the 20s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-06T21:47:00Z — same caveat): Saturday showers most persistent in New York — Tonight will be quiet, with a partly to mostly cloudy sky and lows on either side of 50 degrees. This weekend turns much cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back closer to 50. Expect lots of clouds with a few additional showers, especially on Saturday. The rain could be steadier in both New York and southern Vermont on Saturday evening. Sunday looks drier, with morning clouds giving way to a window of afternoon sun — which may illuminate a light dusting of summit snow. Most of next week will be chilly and overcast with highs in the 40s, plus a few chances for showers and minor mountain snow accumulations.
